newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia sees steady economic growth in 1997.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia sees steady economic growth in 1997.

text.p: Indonesia expects continued steady economic growth in 1997 after recording a satisfactory 7.82 percent growth rate in 1996, Planning Minister Ginanjar Kartasasmita said on Thursday.
"The growth rate of 7.82 percent is satisfying. Although it was slower than the revised growth figure of 8.21 percent in 1995," Ginanjar told reporters after meeting President Suharto.
He said economic growth in 1995 had been revised up to 8.21 percent from 8.1 percent, but did not give any reasons.
"We want steady economic growth in 1997 at around the 1996 level. I predict economic growth in 1997 at between 7.5 to 7.8 percent," Ginanjar said.
"We have predicted that 1996 economic growth will be below the 1995 level, but the figure is still far higher than the annual target of 7.1 percent," Ginanjar said.
He said per capita income rose to $1,140 in 1996 from $1,039 the previous year.
He said the manufacturing industry sector grew by 11.03 percent in 1996, compared with 10.81 percent in 1995.
Growth in the electricity, gas and clean water sectors was 12.61 percent in 1996, against 15.51 percent in 1995.
The building materials sector grew by 12.37 percent, compared with 12.02 percent in 1995, while financial and corporate services expanded 10.52 percent, against 11.22 percent in 1995.
He said the trade, hotel and restaurant sectors grew by 7.63 percent, mining by 7.13 percent, while agriculture, fisheries, animal husbandry and forestry rose by 1.89 percent.
Ginanjar said the government's aim was not to create the highest rate of economic growth possible but to give attention to economic stability as well.
"Pushing economic growth to the highest level could create victims in other sectors, for example, by widening the current account deficit," Ginanjar said.
Indonesia has said its current account deficit is expected to rise to $9.8 billion in fiscal 1997/98 (April-March) from $8.8 billion in fiscal 1996/97.

The head of the Central Bureau of Statistics, Sugito, said manufacturing industries made up the largest sector of the economy, contributing 25.16 percent of the 1996 total. The share of the agricultural sector was 16.30 percent.
Sugito said household consumption grew 9.20 percent in 1996, compared with 9.73 percent in 1995.
Ginanjar said the government would continue to control inflation and to have prudent economic management policies.
"We will continue to control inflation in 1997. I think inflation will be around five to six percent in 1997," he said.
Indonesia's annual inflation rate in 1996 was 6.47 percent.
